<!-- generated from skills/legal-privacy/legal-documents/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# legal-documents

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D14 Legal & Privacy (LG)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng
- **Depends on:** privacy-laws, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** cookie-consent, dsar-handling, compliance-audit, audit-trails

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** drafting or updating the terms of service, privacy notice, or cookie policy; publishing a new document version; recording acceptance at signup or on a material change; checking published documents against the data inventory, processor register, and feature list.
- **Do NOT use when:** the document needs a legal decision — a novel clause, a contested rights position, sector-regulated wording. This skill drafts from the product's own registers and marks the output as a draft for qualified counsel; it never gives legal advice and never presents a generated document as reviewed law (LG-070).

## Rules

1. **LG-061 — Documents derive from the registers, or not at all.** Terms, the privacy notice, and the cookie policy are generated from this product's data inventory/RoPA, processor register, and feature list — never from a generic template. If a register input is missing or stale, the skill stops and names the gap instead of drafting around it.
2. **LG-062 — The notice carries the full information set.** The privacy notice states everything GDPR Articles 13/14 require — controller identity and contact, purposes, lawful basis per purpose, data categories, recipients/processors, transfers, retention, the rights available and how to exercise them — in plain language per Article 12(1).
3. **LG-063 — Every version is stored in full.** Each published version has a version ID and an effective date, and its complete text is archived at publication. Superseded versions remain retrievable: a dispute is answered with the exact text that user accepted.
4. **LG-064 — Acceptance is an event, not a sentence.** Acceptance is stored as a record — user, document, version, timestamp, mechanism — captured at signup. "By using this site you agree" with no stored record does not count as acceptance.
5. **LG-065 — Material changes are noticed and re-accepted.** A material change (new purpose, processor, or data category; a change to user rights or to how data is shared) is published as a new version with an effective date and a change notice, and existing users pass a re-acceptance flow before the new version binds them.
6. **LG-066 — Documents trail the registers, mechanically.** A new processor, data category, or purpose without a corresponding document update blocks release. A register change produces a document diff for review; the notice's processor and data-category lists are the same data as the registers, rendered — not a second hand-maintained copy.
7. **LG-067 — Template residue is a defect class.** A published document contains no other company's name, no bracketed or unfilled placeholders, and no product or feature names that are not this product's.
8. **LG-068 — Annexes attach only when the feature exists.** Sector and feature annexes (payments, user-generated content, minors) are included only while the feature ships. An annex for a removed or unbuilt feature is removed in the same release that removes the feature.
9. **LG-069 — Written for the user who must act on it.** Documents name this product and its controller, use defined terms consistently, and state every contact and rights route exactly as it works in the product. Copy a non-lawyer cannot parse fails, however complete it is.
10. **LG-070 — Counsel review is a recorded step.** The initial version and every material change carry draft status until a qualified legal review is recorded (reviewer, date, version reviewed). Publication before that record exists is a release defect, not a shortcut.
11. **LG-071 — Every route named in a document is live.** The privacy contact, the DSAR intake route, and any opt-out path named in a document are monitored and working. A document that routes a rights request to an unmonitored address or a dead form is a false statement, not a typo.
12. **LG-072 — The live text is the version of record.** The published page is identical to the archived version it claims to be. Corrections and edits ship as a new version under LG-063/LG-065; nobody edits a live document in place.

## BAN list

- **BAN-LG-031 — Notice describes another product's practices.** Banned: a privacy notice that names data the product does not collect, or omits data it does, because the text came from a template or a similar product. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: generate every practice statement from the data inventory and processor register, and fail loudly on a missing register input (LG-061). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-032 — Foreign names and placeholders in published text.** Banned: publishing a document containing another company's name, a bracketed placeholder such as `[Company Name]`, or a template's example product. Defeats: DET-CON-017. Instead: run the residue lint (G-LG-032) and fill every field from this product's own records before publication (LG-067). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-033 — Agreement claimed with no acceptance record.** Banned: relying on "by using this site you agree" (or an equivalent sentence) as the only evidence of acceptance — no stored version, no timestamp, no mechanism. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: store the acceptance event at signup and on material change, and answer disputes from the archive (LG-064, LG-063). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-034 — Silent in-place change of a binding document.** Banned: editing live terms or a live notice — new clause, same version ID and effective date — with no change notice and no re-acceptance. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: publish a new version with a new effective date, notify users, and run the re-acceptance flow for material changes (LG-065, LG-072). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-035 — Versions of a document that contradict each other.** Banned: serving different markets, locales, or surfaces different live versions of the same document whose substance disagrees (different processors named, different retention stated). Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: one version of record per document, translations generated from it, and the diff gate run across every served variant (LG-066, G-LG-031). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-LG-031 — Document-vs-register diff.** Verifies: LG-061, LG-066. Check (automated): in CI, extract the processor names and data categories named in the privacy notice and diff them against the processor register and the RoPA; repeat for every served locale/surface variant. Pass: zero names or categories present in one source and absent from the other. Fail: block shipment until the register or the document is corrected. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-032 — Template-residue lint.** Verifies: LG-067. Check (automated): scan the publishable document set for bracketed placeholders (`\[…\]`, `{{…}}`, "Lorem", "TODO"), and for any organization or product name not in the project's approved-names list from the fact-sheet. Pass: zero hits. Fail: block publication. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-033 — Acceptance-record test.** Verifies: LG-064, LG-065. Check (automated): create a test account in staging and assert an acceptance row exists carrying user ID, document ID, version, timestamp, and mechanism; then publish a test material change and assert the re-acceptance prompt fires and its acceptance is recorded as a second row. Pass: both rows exist with all fields. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-034 — Version-archive integrity check.** Verifies: LG-063, LG-072. Check (automated): hash each live legal page and compare against the archived text of the version it declares; assert every superseded version's full text is present in the archive. Pass: every live hash matches its declared version and the archive is complete. Fail: block shipment — the live page is replaced from the archive or republished as a new version. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-035 — Counsel-review and live-read check.** Verifies: LG-070, LG-062, LG-071. Check (manual): confirm a counsel-review record (reviewer, date, version) exists for the current version and each material change, with no version published while in draft status; then read the live privacy notice against the data inventory end to end and exercise each contact and rights route it names. Pass: review records complete, no practice in the inventory missing from the notice or vice versa, every named route answers. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Documents are rendered from the registers, never written from a template.
- Acceptance is a stored event: user, version, timestamp, mechanism.
- A material change means a new version, a notice, and re-acceptance.
- The live page is byte-identical to the archived version it claims to be.
- Every document ships as a draft until counsel review is recorded.

## Checklist

- [ ] Terms, privacy notice, and cookie policy generated from the current data inventory, processor register, and feature list (LG-061, G-LG-031).
- [ ] Privacy notice carries the full Articles 13/14 information set in plain language (LG-062).
- [ ] Current version archived in full with version ID and effective date; superseded versions retrievable (LG-063, G-LG-034).
- [ ] Acceptance events stored at signup with user, version, timestamp, mechanism (LG-064, G-LG-033).
- [ ] Material changes published as new versions with change notice and re-acceptance (LG-065).
- [ ] Residue lint clean: no foreign names, placeholders, or clauses for unshipped features (LG-067, LG-068, G-LG-032).
- [ ] Counsel-review record exists for the current version; no version published in draft status (LG-070, G-LG-035).
- [ ] Every contact and rights route named in the documents tested live (LG-071).

<!-- generated from skills/legal-privacy/licensing/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# licensing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D14 Legal & Privacy (LG)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://spdx.org/licenses/ ; https://choosealicense.com/
- **Depends on:** none — standalone: license checks read the actual license texts of the dependencies, fonts, images, and datasets being added — primary legal sources, not another skill's output. Its verdicts feed compliance-audit and legal-documents.
- **Feeds into:** compliance-audit, legal-documents

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** adding any dependency, font, image, dataset, or copied snippet; vendoring third-party code; preparing a release (SBOM and notices); choosing or changing the project's own LICENSE; reviewing whether an asset's terms permit the intended use, including transfer to a client or a rebuild.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is a contested rights call — disputed ownership, a license whose terms are ambiguous for the intended use, a takedown or infringement claim. This skill records provenance and applies the written tier policy; it never interprets a license for a contested case or gives legal advice (LG-112).

## Rules

1. **LG-101 — Every component is inventoried.** Every shipped component — library, font, image, dataset, copied snippet — has an inventory row recording its name, version, origin, and license as an SPDX License List identifier (e.g. `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `GPL-3.0-only`), so policy is machine-checkable instead of name-matching prose. A component with no row does not ship.
2. **LG-102 — Provenance is recorded at adoption time.** The inventory row is written when the component is adopted: where it came from, where its license text lives, and the adoption date. An asset whose provenance cannot be established is treated as unlicensed until proven otherwise.
3. **LG-103 — "No license found" is forbidden-tier.** Absence of a license is not permission: default copyright means all rights reserved. A component with no license found is replaced, or the rights holder's written permission is obtained and filed with the inventory row.
4. **LG-104 — Tiers are set per distribution model.** The project's written license policy defines three tiers — allowed (permissive), review (weak or file-level copyleft), forbidden without a written exception (strong/network copyleft in a distribution model it infects, non-commercial terms, no license found) — separately for each way the product ships (hosted service vs. distributed artifact). The same library can be allowed in one model and forbidden in the other; the tier is decided against the actual model, never in the abstract.
5. **LG-105 — Review-tier items get a named decision.** Every review-tier component carries a recorded decision: the decider's name, the date, the distribution model considered, and the reasoning. An undecided review-tier component does not ship.
6. **LG-106 — Exceptions are written and expire.** A forbidden-tier exception names the component, the reason, the approver, and a review date. An exception past its review date is void until re-approved; a verbal exception does not exist.
7. **LG-107 — Vendored code keeps its license files.** Vendored code, fonts, and assets keep their license and copyright files intact in the tree. Stripping them is a defect found by scan (G-LG-054), not a cleanup step.
8. **LG-108 — Notices are generated, never hand-written.** Attribution is discharged by a notices file generated from the inventory and shipped with the product; where a license triggers a copyleft source-offer duty, the offer is implemented as a real download or disclosure of the corresponding source, not a link to upstream. A notices entry with no inventory row, or a shipped component with no notices entry, is a defect.
9. **LG-109 — An SBOM is emitted per release.** Each release emits an SBOM (SPDX or CycloneDX format) from the build, and the SBOM, the inventory, and the notices file are diffed against each other (G-LG-052). The OpenChain ISO/IEC 5230 program elements are the reference for what the compliance program contains.
10. **LG-110 — Licensing is a CI property.** Adding or upgrading a component re-runs the scan and inventory update in the same change. Licensing is never a launch-week audit reconstructed from memory.
11. **LG-111 — The project's own LICENSE is chosen deliberately.** At project creation a LICENSE is selected deliberately (Choose a License is the selection aid), names this project and its rights holder, and matches the intended distribution. No LICENSE file means nobody — including future collaborators — has permission to use the code.
12. **LG-112 — Transferability is checked; contested calls escalate.** Before an asset ships in client work or a rebuild, its terms are checked for transferability (e.g. stock and font licenses that do not transfer). Where the rights position is ambiguous or contested, work on that asset stops and the call goes to qualified counsel with the inventory record attached.

## BAN list

- **BAN-LG-051 — Vendored material shipped with its license files stripped.** Banned: dropping vendored code, a font, or an asset into the tree with its LICENSE, COPYING, or copyright notices deleted. Defeats: DET-CON-020. Instead: keep the license and copyright files with the vendored copy and add the inventory row (LG-101, LG-107). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-052 — "Fully licensed" claimed with no inventory behind it.** Banned: stating in product copy, a client deliverable, or a store listing that all assets or components are licensed or rights-cleared when no inventory and tier record exists to prove it. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: make the claim only for what the inventory covers, component by component, or do not make it (LG-101, LG-102). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-053 — A LICENSE file that names another project.** Banned: copying a LICENSE from a tutorial, template, or another repository so the shipped file names the wrong project or rights holder. Defeats: DET-CON-017. Instead: choose the license deliberately for this project and put this project's name and rights holder in it (LG-111). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-054 — A component shipped because "no license" was read as "free to use."** Banned: shipping a library, snippet, font, or dataset for which no license was found, on the reasoning that public availability implies permission. Defeats: DET-CON-020. Instead: treat no-license-found as forbidden-tier — replace the component or file the rights holder's written permission (LG-103). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-055 — Notices or license claims that contradict the inventory.** Banned: publishing a notices file, attribution page, or compliance claim (e.g. "OpenChain conformant") that the inventory and scan results do not support, or leaving a generated notices file stale after components change. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: regenerate notices from the inventory at release and implement triggered duties as real disclosures (LG-108, LG-109). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-LG-051 — CI license scan.** Verifies: LG-101, LG-103, LG-104. Check (automated): run a source-level scan (ScanCode Toolkit) plus the ecosystem metadata checker (`license-checker`, `pip-licenses`, or `cargo-deny`) over the full tree, including vendored directories; compare every detected SPDX identifier against the policy tiers for the target distribution model. Pass: no forbidden-tier identifier, no unlisted identifier, and no component detected that lacks an inventory row. Fail: block the build. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-052 — SBOM–inventory–notices diff.** Verifies: LG-108, LG-109. Check (automated): emit the release SBOM (SPDX or CycloneDX) and diff its component set against the inventory and the generated notices file. Pass: the three sets are identical. Fail: block shipment until the missing row or notices entry exists. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-053 — Provenance completeness lint.** Verifies: LG-101, LG-102. Check (automated): lint the inventory — every row must carry a non-empty SPDX identifier, origin, license-text location, and adoption date; a row marked "unknown" in any field fails. Pass: zero incomplete rows. Fail: block shipment; the component is provenanced, replaced, or removed. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-054 — Vendored-file integrity scan.** Verifies: LG-107. Check (automated): for every vendored directory, assert a LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE file (or the upstream license text recorded in the inventory) is present and non-empty. Pass: every vendored component retains its license material. Fail: block shipment and restore the files from upstream. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-055 — Decision and exception register review.** Verifies: LG-105, LG-106, LG-112. Check (manual): read the decision register — every review-tier component in the inventory has a named decision with reasoning; every exception names component, reason, approver, and a review date that has not passed; every client/rebuild asset has a recorded transferability check or an escalation entry. Pass: all three hold in writing. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- No license found means no permission — default copyright applies.
- Unknown provenance is unlicensed until proven otherwise.
- Every component: SPDX ID, origin, tier — recorded when adopted, not at launch.
- Notices are generated from the inventory, never hand-written.
- Tier follows the distribution model: the same library can be allowed hosted and forbidden shipped.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every shipped component has an inventory row with SPDX identifier, origin, and adoption date (LG-101, LG-102, G-LG-053).
- [ ] No component with no license found is shipped without filed written permission (LG-103, BAN-LG-054).
- [ ] Every review-tier component has a named, reasoned decision; every exception is written and in date (LG-105, LG-106, G-LG-055).
- [ ] Vendored code and assets retain their license and copyright files (LG-107, G-LG-054).
- [ ] The release SBOM, inventory, and shipped notices diff clean (LG-108, LG-109, G-LG-052).
- [ ] The CI license scan passes for the target distribution model (LG-104, G-LG-051).
- [ ] The project's own LICENSE names this project, and client/rebuild assets have a transferability check or escalation on record (LG-111, LG-112).

# privacy-laws

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D14 Legal & Privacy (LG)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng ; https://cy.ico.org.uk/for-organisations/advice-and-services/audits/data-protection-audit-framework/toolkits/accountability/records-of-processing-and-lawful-basis/
- **Depends on:** fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** legal-documents, cookie-consent, dsar-handling, data-residency, compliance-audit

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a product enters a market, adds a feature, data category, user type, or processor; building or re-verifying the obligations register, the data map (RoPA), the lawful-basis register, or the retention schedule; deciding whether a processing purpose may be built at all.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question needs a legal decision — novel processing, children's, health, finance, or biometric data, a contested rights call, regulator contact. This skill produces engineering artifacts for qualified counsel to confirm; it never gives legal advice and never declares a product compliant (LG-011).

## Rules

1. **LG-001 — Register before features.** Before build, enumerate markets served × data categories processed × user types in the obligations register; each cell records the governing regime, the obligations it creates, and the product requirement satisfying each. A market or feature with no register row does not ship.
2. **LG-002 — The register is data, not prose.** Register rows carry: market, regime, obligation, requirement, owner, lawful basis, last-verified date, review date. If coverage cannot be checked mechanically from the table, the register is an essay and fails.
3. **LG-003 — Lawful basis per purpose.** Every processing purpose has a recorded lawful basis (GDPR Article 6, or the applicable regime's equivalent permission) assigned per purpose, never per product, before the purpose is built.
4. **LG-004 — The data map is the source.** Every personal-data category in the data map (RoPA) has a purpose, a lawful basis, and a retention period; the register derives from the data map, and the two never disagree silently — a mismatch is a defect in one of them.
5. **LG-005 — Minimisation at the schema level.** A form field, column, or event property with no registered purpose is removed from the form and schema, not excused in policy prose.
6. **LG-006 — Triggers are tested, not assumed.** DPIA triggers (GDPR Article 35) and DPO/representative triggers (Articles 37–39) are tested explicitly for each product and the outcome recorded, including "not triggered, because…" with the reasoning.
7. **LG-007 — Retention is a schedule, not an intention.** Every data category has a retention period in the register and a deletion or anonymisation mechanism that actually runs; "kept as long as needed" is not a retention period.
8. **LG-008 — Variance is stated, never averaged.** Where regimes conflict (e.g. a retention duty against an erasure right), the conflict is logged in the register and escalated to counsel; nobody resolves it by picking the convenient rule.
9. **LG-009 — Every legal statement is dated and sourced.** Each register row names its source and last-verified date; a row past its review date is treated as unverified and blocks reliance until re-verified.
10. **LG-010 — Scope is explicit.** Deep profiles ship for GDPR and CCPA/CPRA only. Every other regime is a register-format entry marked "register before serving"; no output implies coverage the register does not contain.
11. **LG-011 — Escalation stops are hard stops.** Children's products, health/finance data, biometric processing, novel processing, contested rights calls, and any regulator contact stop the work: the output is the artifact set plus "this needs qualified counsel." The skill never declares a product "GDPR compliant" or equivalent.
12. **LG-012 — Change re-derives the register.** A new market, feature, processor, data category, or user type triggers a register update before release; the register is re-run on change, not on an annual ritual.

## BAN list

- **BAN-LG-001 — Compliance claimed without a tested process.** Banned: publishing "GDPR compliant", "fully compliant", or an equivalent badge in marketing, docs, or the product when no tested control supports the exact wording. Defeats: DET-CON-012. Instead: publish only what a dated audit artifact proves, worded as what was tested, when, and against what (LG-011). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-002 — Privacy artifacts copied from another product.** Banned: a data map, register, or notice derived from a template or another product's documents instead of this product's own inventory. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: derive every row from this product's data map and feature list (LG-001, LG-004). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-003 — Erasure on paper, hiding in the product.** Banned: recording an erasure right or retention limit in the register while the implemented flow only hides the profile or flags the record and keeps the data reachable. Defeats: DET-FAKE-011. Instead: implement erasure against the stores the register names, verified by a residue check (LG-007). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-004 — Rights promised with no process behind them.** Banned: a privacy notice or register that promises access, erasure, or objection rights while no working intake and handling flow exists. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: ship the intake channel, the clock, and the handling flow first, then write the promise (LG-001). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-LG-005 — Regime values hardcoded as eternal constants.** Banned: baking a consent age, a response clock, or an adequacy status into code or copy as an undated constant with no source or review date. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: keep every such value in the dated, sourced register table and read it as per-market configuration (LG-009). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-LG-001 — Register coverage check.** Verifies: LG-001, LG-003. Check (automated): script the register against product config and the data map — every market in config and every processing purpose in the data map must have a register row with non-empty regime, lawful-basis, and owner fields. Pass: zero uncovered markets or purposes. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-002 — Data-map completeness check.** Verifies: LG-004, LG-005, LG-007. Check (automated): every data-map row asserts a stated purpose, lawful basis, and retention period; every personal-data field found in schemas and forms (`grep` the schema/form definitions against the data map's category list) maps to a data-map row. Pass: no category missing a basis or retention, no unmapped field. Fail: block shipment — the unmapped field is removed or registered first. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-003 — Review-date lint.** Verifies: LG-009. Check (automated): scan the register for rows whose review date is earlier than today. Pass: zero stale rows. Fail: block reliance on the stale rows until re-verified against their sources; the compliance-audit checklist stays open meanwhile. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-004 — Processor tripwire.** Verifies: LG-012. Check (automated): diff the dependency/SDK list and third-party endpoints in the build against the register's processor rows. Pass: every processor in the build has a register row. Fail: block shipment — a new analytics or processor SDK with no row is unregistered processing. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-LG-005 — Trigger and escalation review.** Verifies: LG-006, LG-008, LG-011. Check (manual): read the register's trigger section and conflict log — every DPIA/DPO trigger test has a recorded outcome, every regime conflict has an escalation entry, and every LG-011 stop condition is either absent (with the check recorded) or escalated to counsel. Pass: all three hold in writing. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- No register row, no ship: markets and purposes are enumerated before build.
- Lawful basis is per purpose, never per product.
- A field with no purpose is deleted, not policy-washed.
- Conflicts are logged and escalated, never averaged away.
- This skill builds artifacts for counsel; it never declares compliance.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every market, feature, and user type has a register row (LG-001, G-LG-001).
- [ ] Every processing purpose has a recorded lawful basis (LG-003).
- [ ] Every data-map category states purpose, lawful basis, and retention period (LG-004, LG-007, G-LG-002).
- [ ] No form or schema field lacks a registered purpose (LG-005).
- [ ] DPIA and DPO trigger tests recorded, including negative outcomes (LG-006, G-LG-005).
- [ ] No register row is past its review date (LG-009, G-LG-003).
- [ ] No LG-011 stop condition is un-escalated; no public compliance claim lacks a tested control (LG-011, BAN-LG-001).
